answerable: Sensitivity of surface runoff vs. deep drainage (recharge) partitioning to soil clay fraction under identical climate forcing
Relative changes in infiltration, saturated hydraulic conductivity, and soil moisture storage across a clay gradient
Monotonic trend and possible thresholds in runoff/recharge ratio as clay increases from 5% to 55%
not_answerable: Absolute field-validated runoff values for any specific real watershed (no site observations provided)
Effects of clay mineralogy, macropore/preferential flow, or shrink-swell dynamics not represented in default ELM hydrology
Lateral subsurface flow and hillslope routing (single-column has no lateral connectivity)

parsed.n_justification: A controlled single-factor sweep of clay content requires identical forcing and geometry across columns, varying only the clay fraction. Six columns span 5%,15%,25%,35%,45%,55% clay in equal 10% increments, giving adequate resolution to detect nonlinear thresholds in runoff/recharge partitioning while keeping the ensemble compact and interpretable.
requires_capabilities: Surface dataset / cold-start modification to override clay (PCT_CLAY) in each column while holding sand-adjusted texture and all other parameters fixed
assumptions: All columns share identical atmospheric forcing, PFT, topography (STD_ELEV/SLOPE), and soil depth; only PCT_CLAY (and complementary sand to conserve mass) is varied
Sand content adjusted to keep silt roughly constant so texture shifts along the sand-clay axis; organic matter held fixed
Clay fraction is applied uniformly across all soil layers to isolate its effect
First ~5 years treated as spin-up/warm-up and excluded from partitioning analysis; multi-year climatology used to average out interannual variability
Recharge is diagnosed from bottom-layer drainage (QDRAI/QCHARGE) and runoff from QOVER+QRGWL, with no lateral flow in single-column mode
Default ELM Clapp-Hornberger/pedotransfer functions translate clay fraction into hydraulic properties (Ksat, porosity, matric potential)
